industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares at EUR 69.40 (2026-10-02), bullish on the business. The record's recommendation is to park with an entry level of about EUR 50, the 'defendable' 15x band on today's 24-month-forward earnings, at which the eighteen-month modal return clears the framework's 20 percent a year bar; the re-look is after the Q3 2026 periodic information on 9 October 2026 (the backlog against intake) and the FY2026 result. Conviction is medium on the business view (the thesis is evidenced through every layer of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain) and medium on the price view (the de-rating is probable, its timing is not). The gate line does not park the case: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) B, business quality (E 2, BB 2) C, predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) B, trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) C, no D or F; the return parks it. The thesis in one line: LU-VE is a demand-inflection case in a mid-margin component manufacturer; data-centre and power-generation cooling demand has lifted the orders, the revenue, the margin and the sell-side's estimates, and the company built the capacity in the right place in time to take it; at EUR 69.40 the shares already pay for that delivery and for a multiple the stock has never held for long, so the business is worth owning and the price is not. 'Modal return' on the framework's convention: -3.4 percent a year over eighteen months (value including cash returns EUR 65.88 at 2028-04-02) and +1.3 percent a year over three years (EUR 72.06 at 2029-10-02), from a reference price of EUR 69.40 on 2026-10-02; rated F. Even at the current 20.8x held throughout, about 13 percent a year, a C, which the record calls the ceiling of the case from this price without a second hyperscaler contract. The drop-through sensitivity (tax 25 percent, interest flat, depreciation EUR 36m) cuts FY2028 EPS to about EUR 2.88 from EUR 3.38, 15 percent lower, keeps the rating F and lowers the eighteen-month entry level to about EUR 43.
case: The change is external, structural and sector-wide. The AI-driven data-centre build-out, through the shift to high-temperature liquid cooling at the rack that rejects more heat outdoors per megawatt, and the power-generation infrastructure that feeds it, have lifted demand for the large dry coolers and air-cooled equipment LU-VE makes; the disruption the market feared (liquid cooling eliminating dry coolers) is being disproved and reversed into a multiplier (KQ 3, RA 1, E 1, BB 1 B). The force shows across the peer set (Alfa Laval orders +29 percent in Q2 2026; Carel H1 2026 revenue +20.9 percent to EUR 370.1m; Kelvion's data-centre business over half its mix and growing over 50 percent; lead times 20 to 30 weeks; Morgan Stanley's liquid-cooling market growth over 50 percent a year to 2028) and passes the 'Demand Inflection' test at A (KQ 1, RA 1, E 1, BB 1). A second engine is contractual: the revised EU F-Gas Regulation (ban on new units above 150 GWP including R-32 from January 2027; HFC quota to 11 percent in 2027) and the US AIM Act move demand towards the natural-refrigerant products that are 58 percent of turnover (KQ 4 B). The company's own cycle has turned (KQ 6 B: revenue -4.6 percent FY2024, +2.8 percent FY2025, +10.3 percent H1 2026; refrigeration +9.0 percent in Q2 2026 after a flat Q1; heat-pump components recovered after a 65 percent fall in FY2024). Two external forces are headwinds (competition in European heat pumps, with Midea's EU exports +60 percent targeting 15 percent share from 4 to 5 percent, KQ 2 C; the political side of regulation, subsidy rollback in Germany and the UK), landing on the Components SBU, half the group; supply is neutral on profit and a headwind in kind (copper +10 percent in H1 2026; price contribution EUR 5.1m against EUR 7.7m of raw-material cost; EC motors from two manufacturers; KQ 5 C); macro neutral (KQ 7 C); trade policy hedged by Texas (KQ 8 C). External forces B.

The company's own change is a capacity choice made in time, not a transformation. Same chief executive, strategy and structure; the Jacksonville plant doubled to over 30,000 square metres and inaugurated in May 2026, a month after the framework agreement of over EUR 100m with a global hyperscaler (April 2026). Four internal forces strong: guidance raised twice (KQ 4, RA 2 A), the US as a new geography (KQ 7 A), data-centre dry coolers, the Alfa V Mega range and CO2 data-centre systems as a new product application (KQ 8 B; Paterna, Spain; a Swedish operator at EUR 7.45m), strategy articulated and resourced with capex to EUR 30m to 35m a year (KQ 3 B), standards improving on margin while lagging on cash (KQ 5 B). No red flags. No chief-executive change (KQ 1 C), leadership consolidations rather than new actors (KQ 2 C), nominal formula-driven pricing not real (KQ 9 C), no acquisition step (KQ 10 C; four deals since 2015 at an average 7.0x EBITDA), falling balance-sheet use (KQ 11 C; EUR 250m of firepower on TPICAP's estimate), a smooth progressive dividend (KQ 12 C), safety stock replacing just-in-time (KQ 13 C). Internal forces B; not A because the change is organic and capacity-led rather than multi-dimensional. Change Forces (E 1, BB 1) B.

'Financial Outputs' have moved through every layer. Key metrics B (revenue growth A; margin B with consensus 15.1, 15.8, 16.2, 17.0 percent for FY2026 to FY2029 and not A because the level is below the 20 percent "solid" line; net debt B; cash conversion C, free cash flow 74 percent of net income in FY2025 against 145 percent in FY2024, operating working capital 18.6 percent of sales). Goldilocks growth B: modal EPS growth about 25 percent over six months, 23 percent a year over eighteen months, 21 percent a year over three years, above the 12 to 20 percent band in the 20 to 30 percent band the framework calls "fine but riskier", and FY2028 consensus growth of 15.5 percent already shows the normalisation. Sell-side upgrades B: the record's modal FY2026 EPS EUR 2.40 is 2.6 percent above the EUR 2.34 consensus median (KQ 1 B); guidance is not above consensus, a floor the market has priced through (KQ 2 C); the upgrade record is A (11 percent organic revenue CAGR since the 2015 IPO against 5 to 6 percent guided; the "conservative sandbagger"; the one miss FY2024); the revision skew is A (FY2027 mean from EUR 2.19 to EUR 3.02; five of five Buy or Overweight); the dashboard revisions B with the one negative the buy share down 17 points; the sell-side calls the guide conservative and sees upgrades "largely in FY2027" (KQ 6 B); not A because consensus already embeds low-double-digit growth and a 15.8 percent FY2027 margin, so the next upgrades need delivery. Staircase B: near steps (Q3 2026 on 9 October 2026; the FY2026 result; the first EUR 20m of hyperscaler revenue in H2 2026; Chillventa 2026) B; mid steps (the bulk of hyperscaler execution in FY2027; Jacksonville staffing; the trade-fair cycle; possible acquisitions; the long-term incentive's 15 percent US EBITDA weight) B; far steps (the 2029 plan targets; the 2027 F-Gas ban; the 4 million heat-pump target for 2030) C, broadly understood. Financial Outputs (E 2, BB 1) B.
counter_case: At its strongest, LU-VE is a false friend. The backlog and the growth are real, but they are bought with cash the business does not generate: days sales outstanding have risen from 51 (2023) to 63 (2024) to 73 (2025); days in inventory from 62 to 66 and now 83 in H1 2026; the cushion is a payables stretch to 158 days on 120-day terms that a supplier can reverse; operating cash flow was negative EUR 12.1m in Q1 2026. The hyperscaler contract was won on lead time in a product the experts call increasingly commoditised ("the primary driver for winning large accounts is lead time and local capacity rather than technical differentiation or price"); the hyperscaler may be over 15 percent of revenue by FY2027, and it leaves when Kelvion, Modine and Vertiv's new capacity arrives. The FY2027 step is a one-contract event priced as a franchise, in a family-controlled company where the minority has no lever and the strategic bench is three people. The shares at the 97th percentile of their own history are the market making the Risks report's mistake in reverse. The record concedes: the margin structure (adjusted EBIT 10.8 percent, gross margin 20 percent, return on invested capital about 12.5 percent) is that of a component maker, not a franchise; the working-capital trend through 2025 was adverse and the H1 2026 inventory build is real; the EC motor dependence is unmitigated beyond stock; the position in data centres rests on capacity timing; and the price is wrong. The record's answer on the business: H1 2026 cash flow from operations rose 31 percent to EUR 39.8m and leverage fell to 0.7x, which a false friend does not do; the inventory build is a stated choice to secure delivery of a backlog 48 percent larger, with mid-teens working capital guided and the exclusions named; pass-through pricing held absolute EBITDA through a 10 percent copper rise; the refrigeration cycle turned in Q2 2026; the 2023 to 2024 heat-pump collapse produced record EBITDA on lower sales. The bear case's conclusion, hold and watch, is the record's as well, reached by the price rather than the cash; its monitorables (working capital above 18 percent of sales; three negative cash-flow quarters) are in the monitoring table.

Against the price verdict (BB 4): the case is robust at this price because the data-centre re-rating is structural; the market now values cooling as infrastructure rather than a weather trade (Huatai); data-centre-exposed peers trade at over 20x EV/EBITDA (TPICAP); LU-VE at about 16x FY2026 and 13x FY2027 EV/EBITDA is the cheap way in, so the mark-to-market risk is to the upside; the stock's own ten-year P/E history is the wrong yardstick because the business it describes was half refrigeration. The record's answer: an EV/EBITDA discount to pure plays exists and a floor above the ten-year median is conceded for the mix; but a 10.8 percent adjusted EBIT margin, 45 percent refrigeration mix and 12.5 percent return on invested capital do not earn a pure-play multiple (Carel 22.5 percent EBITDA margin; Kelvion 15 to 17 percent, and the 20x-plus peers are the ones with the margins); the stock's own 24-month-forward history, which embeds its own mix, says 20.8x is a level it has visited and left (five-year high 23.50x, median 14.49x); the framework's caution that multiples fall further than people accept ex ante applies with force to a stock up 94 percent in a year; if the premium is structural it will still be there at EUR 50, and if it is not, EUR 69.40 is the wrong price to find out.
triggers: What the record said would change the view, item by item. The FY2027 earnings step (70 percent probable at or above EUR 2.90 adjusted EPS, reported by March 2028): a Q3 2026 backlog below EUR 300m on 9 October 2026, or H2 2026 US sales without the EUR 20m hyperscaler contribution; Invalidate on the backlog below EUR 250m at any quarter; Alarm on US product sales growth below 40 percent in H2 2026, Invalidate on hyperscaler revenue below EUR 20m in H2 2026. The multiple (the cleared branch at about 45 percent): a widening of the hyperscaler relationship, a second framework or the first extended beyond EUR 100m, would make the premium a function of a repeatable position rather than one contract and is the upside not priced; Alarm at 22x 24-month-forward (the five-year high was 23.50x); the entry level about EUR 50, where the multiple is 15.0x; the first thing to watch is the market catching up with the valuation concern (KQ 7, RA 1, E 1, BB 4), since that catch-up is the de-rating the modal case assumes. Cash conversion (60 percent that operating working capital returns below 17 percent of sales by FY2027): Alarm above 20 percent of sales; Invalidate above 22 percent for two consecutive quarters, or three consecutive quarters of negative operating cash flow (the Risks report's own trigger). The refrigeration and heat-pump cycle (75 percent that refrigeration applications grow in H2 2026): Alarm below 0 percent growth in H2 2026; Invalidate on two consecutive halves of decline; the price assumes group growth at low-double digits, which needs this leg at mid-single digits. The margin: Alarm on the adjusted EBITDA margin below 14.5 percent at FY2026, Invalidate below 14.0 percent. Dated steps: Q3 2026 periodic information 9 October 2026; the FY2026 result (2026-11-12 on FactSet's calendar or March 2027 on the company's pattern); the first EUR 20m of hyperscaler revenue in H2 2026; the bulk of hyperscaler execution in FY2027; Jacksonville staffing towards 200 (8 to 11 skilled operators a month against a baseline of 3 to 5); the F-Gas ban from January 2027; the next weekly thematic run (Master Rating 6 provisional). Open on the inputs: the live thematics file, the track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library were not among the inputs, so the thematic cross-reference rests on the pinned reading and the overlap with own errors is recorded as a possible fit (paying a top-decile multiple for an inflection the sell-side has just finished pricing); the ratings store's reason for Ariston's valuation D against its Master Rating 8 F is not known; the research's cooling peers are not in the store, so no secondary reference set on the eight could be used. Watch items named but not scheduled: the hyperscaler's delivery schedule and US profitability (the long-term incentive's US EBITDA metric disclosed only as achieved or missed); EC motor supply continuity; a further family placing or a change in the loyalty-share arithmetic; the departure of the finance chief or the commercial officer; the Jacksonville return in the 2026 to 2028 incentive. Monitorable series: backlog and intake quarterly; US product sales half-yearly; adjusted EBITDA margin half-yearly; operating working capital quarterly; European heat-pump sales and Chinese EU exports monthly in sell-side trackers; copper and aluminium daily; refrigeration order intake quarterly around the trade-fair cycle; Jacksonville headcount undisclosed.
